title: Effects of Model Scale and Quantization on Social Bias and Abstention in Question Answering
abstract: arXiv:2610.29657v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The deployment of small and quantized language models in resource-constrained settings raises an important fairness question: when a compressed model produces fewer biased responses, does this reflect fairer behavior or greater abstention? We study this problem in Question Answering (QA) using the BBQ benchmark across multiple model sizes and quantization settings from Qwen3, Gemma-3, and SmolLM2. We also examine whether the observed trends remain stable across alternative prompt formulations and when the ``Unknown'' option is removed in a forced-choice setting. Our results show that larger models achieved higher QA accuracy, but bias showed no simple scaling trend and quantization effects varied across configurations. Notably, 20 of the 26 configurations with fewer biased responses also show increased over-abstention, indicating that lower observed bias can partly reflect greater abstention. translated_title: 模型规模与量化对问答任务中社会偏见与弃答行为的影响
translated_abstract: 在资源受限环境中部署小型化和量化语言模型引发了一个重要的公平性问题：当一个压缩后的模型产生更少的有偏见回答时，这反映的是更公平的行为还是更多的弃答？我们在问答任务中使用BBQ基准，对来自Qwen3、Gemma-3和SmolLM2的多种模型规模和量化设置开展了研究。我们还考察了所观察到的趋势在替代提示表述下，以及在强制选择设置中移除“未知”选项时是否保持稳定。结果表明，更大的模型获得了更高的问答准确率，但偏见并未呈现简单的随规模扩展的趋势，且量化的影响因配置而异。值得注意的是，在26个产生较少偏见回答的配置中，有20个同时表现出更高的过度弃答率，这表明观察到的较低偏见可能部分源于更多的弃答。这些发现表明观察到的较低偏见……
tldr: 该研究发现压缩模型观察到的偏见减少可能部分源于弃答增多而非真正更公平——在26个偏见回答较少的配置中，有20个同时表现出过度弃答的增加。
en_tdlr: The study finds that reduced observed bias in compressed and quantized models can partly reflect increased abstention rather than genuine fairness, as 20 of 26 configurations with fewer biased responses also showed increased over-abstention.
